The cache stores frequent lookups in memory and serves them without a database round trip. A request that misses the cache falls through to the source, and the result gets stored for next time. Keys expire after ten minutes by default. Callers can set a shorter or longer window for any given key. The store holds up to two million entries before it evicts the oldest ones first. Metrics report hit rate, eviction count, and average lookup time once a minute. Two processes can share one cache safely, because writes take a single lock per key. The API stays small: get, set, and delete cover almost every case a team runs into.
